To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the number and type of adverse events experienced by patients with traumatic spinal-cord injury (tSCI) are related to patient factors including age, injury severity, and pre-injury health-related conditions, and substance use/withdrawals, and psychiatric conditions; and that delirium risk is higher in patients with tSCI who have substance use/withdrawl comorbidities; and pneumonia risk is higher in those who have a psychiatric condition.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
AEs are common after SCI, with urinary tract infections and pneumonia the most common, and delirium, neuropathic pain, and pressure ulcers also common.

the most common post-injury adverse events in traumatic spinal cord injury are urinary tract infections, pneumonia, neuropathic pain, delirium, and pressure ulcers, and that these events may be related to modifiable comoribidities.
